_note: Per-dataset SPEC-CARD fields. These cards describe THE ATLAS, not the slice we happen to work on: `cells`, `schema` tier counts and `timepoints` are all full-published-object numbers, with `workingSlice` naming our subset where one exists. Joined on `id` to dataset_facts.json (still the source of truth for METHOD/platform and the cluster counts in the summary strip); dataset_facts.json is never modified. Values are read live from the backing .h5ad / author metadata, transcribed from repo prose, or supplied by Steven — see `_provenance`. Anything unsourced is the literal string "TBD". Where a field is not a gap but a genuine absence, it says so in words ("Unannotated — labelling target", "N/A") rather than TBD.

The cells are 14 hpf. Reconciliation is exact: 101,833 (our old concat) - 3,862 (duplicate) + 22,473 (3 dpf) = 120,444. NAMESPACE CLAIM RETRACTED: we recorded Zebrahub as gene-symbol-only and cited that as an integration barrier. Wrong — every original release carries var[gene_ids] with 32,057 ENSDARG plus dTomato/mCerulean/EYFP (Zebrabow transgenes). The early timepoints (10 hpf-24 hpf) span ~17,000-100,000 counts — two QC regimes. UNRESOLVED. REBUILT: zebrahub_combined_v2.h5ad via sources/code/build_zebrahub_combined.py — adopts the authors' full atlas and joins the finer per-stage ZFA labels (154 classes, all 120,444 cells matched), preserving var, layers['counts'] and obsm['X_umap'] with a uns['provenance'] stamp. _provenance.zscape_groups: Grouping derived from the naming convention in obs[gene_target], NOT from a genotype column — none exists. '-mut' suffix = stable mutant line; a hyphen joining two gene symbols = double knockout; bare symbol = single-gene F0 crispant. Corroborated by the data: hgfa/hgfa-mut, mafba/mafba-mut, met/met-mut, noto/noto-mut, tbx16/tbx16-mut all appear as SEPARATE targets (which only makes sense as crispant vs mutant of the same gene), and four of the five mutant genes have a matching sibling control arm (ctrl-hgfa, ctrl-mafba, ctrl-met, ctrl-noto). 18 single + 5 double + 5 mutant = 28.

Each compound has exactly ONE concentration — unlike MegaFin, ChemFish is not a two-dose design. Dosing timepoints from obs[drug_addition] = 6/13/24/36/42 hpf; collection from obs[timepoint] = 36/48/72 hpf. Only the 6 and 13 hpf dosing arms were collected at all three timepoints; 24/36/42 hpf dosing was collected at 48 hpf only.

_provenance.annotation_evidence: ZSCAPE counting reference, SETTLED: GRCz11 with Ensembl release 99 (Danio_rerio.GRCz11.dna.toplevel.fa.gz / Danio_rerio.GRCz11.99.gtf.gz), prepared by the BBI genome pipeline — biotype exclusion then a strand-aware 3' extension of up to 500 bp with same-strand collision clipping — giving 32,031 ENSDARG genes. CODE: bbi-lab/bbi-genome-data (tree 946231a3). organisms/genome.zebrafish.sh names the release, FASTA and GTF; scripts/rna.03.make_bed_files.sh line 4 EXTENSION_LIST="500" and extend_3p_utr_gene_annotations() line 207 implement the extension and clipping. The 500 constant dates to 2020-03-20, predating the 2022-05 deposit. bbi-sci bin/assign-reads-to-genes.py consumes those BEDs. DATA: +strand 3' end median +500, -strand 3' start median -500, 5' ends median 0, max exactly 500 (mean 493 = clipped genes); Ensembl 99 minus pseudogene|IG_*|TR_*|TEC is an EXACT 32,031 set match, 0 discrepancies either way. LAWSON IS RULED OUT — tested directly against the published annotation (eLife 55792 Source Data 2, md5 19759898187c47edfd9c216162851e31, at raw_datasets/_annotations/lawson_v4_3/): 4.54% coordinate agreement (worse than plain Ensembl's 7.34%), bidirectional deltas, and 3,629 ZSCAPE gene ids absent from Lawson entirely. Not a plausible alternative; retained only as a closed negative result. UNRESOLVED: no ZSCAPE-specific run manifest naming the GTF exists — absent from the paper, the GEO series and per-sample records, the bbi-sci docs and the sdg-zfish repo. The transformation is RECONSTRUCTED to exact agreement; the historical manifest is not recovered. CHEMFISH INHERITS IT — CONFIRMED: its cds rowRanges mcols match ZSCAPE's gene metadata on all 32,031 genes for id, ORDER, gene_short_name, chromosome, bp1, bp2 and strand (100.0000%, 0 mismatches in any field). Its Methods independently state read processing and cell filtering followed Saunders et al. 2023. The literal FASTA/GTF filenames are STRONGLY INFERRED by that inheritance: the ChemFish object embeds no reference strings at all.
_provenance.pipeline: How the authors got from raw FASTQ to the object we hold. ZSCAPE — supplied by Steven with citations: bbi-dmux -> bbi-sci (Methods, Nature s41586-023-06720-2), Monocle3 v1.3.1, GEO GSE202639 / SRA SRP374541 / PRJNA836866, repo cole-trapnell-lab/sdg-zfish. That same table also states the GTF is NOT resolvable from the paper or GEO and that Ensembl-vs-Lawson cannot be justified for raw counting — which is why ZSCAPE's annotation stays TBD. GRCz11 downstream gene NAMES do not prove an Ensembl GTF was used for alignment. ChemFish — downstream confirmed LOCALLY, not from the web: the distribution is extracted/chemfish_cds/cds_object.rds with a bpcells_matrix_dir, i.e. a Monocle3 cell_data_set. Raw side unconfirmed; same lab and assay as ZSCAPE makes bbi-dmux/bbi-sci likely but that is inference, so it stays TBD. DanioCell — distributed as a Seurat object (DanioCell site + GEO GSE223922); code at farrelllab/2023_Sur. CellRanger version not confirmed, so raw stays TBD. Zebrahub — TBD. The only pipeline detail findable (Cell Ranger ARC 2.0.2 + Signac) belongs to Zebrahub-MULTIOME, a different assay from the scRNA atlas on this card. Same trap as the genome citation. MiniFin + MegaFin — Parse split-pipe v1.7.1 read from process/run_proc_def.json; downstream from the Trailmaker settings in the design docs (Seurat+Harmony for MiniFin; Seurat then Scanpy for MegaFin). The ZSB build diverges after split-pipe: manual Lawson denoise, then our own Harmony pass. ZSCAPE Commit Gold left TBD deliberately — it is a cut of the same published ZSCAPE data, so it would inherit bbi-dmux/bbi-sci + Monocle3, but that is Steven's call to make rather than mine to assume.
_provenance.zscape_cell_metadata: GSE202639_reference_cell_metadata.csv.gz — 1,241,018 cells x 25 columns, the wild-type REFERENCE arm. Carries per-cell cell_type_sub (~156), cell_type_broad (~98), tissue (33), germ_layer (6), major_group (4), timepoint (19 incl. one blank), expt (GAP13/14/16/18, HF4), embryo, 3D UMAP coords, and gene_target. Note gene_target here has only 7 values: the 6 ctrl-* arms plus tbx16-mut (9,004 cells) — i.e. the reference arm bundles one stable mutant line with the controls, which supports the crispant-vs-stable-mutant split the ZSCAPE card draws from the naming convention. The 28 knockouts live in the zperturb file, not this one.
_provenance.zscape_raw_counts: GSE202639_reference_raw_counts.RDS.gz — dgCMatrix 32,031 x 1,241,018, 523,335,834 non-zeros (98.68% sparse), integer counts max 2,391, 954,711,330 total UMIs, median 454 UMI/cell. Dimensions match the gene and cell metadata exactly. No attributes naming the annotation. File is DOUBLY gzipped (outer gzip around an already-compressed RDS): gunzip first, then readRDS. TWO GAPS CLOSED. (a) The 32,031-gene set is the REFERENCE, not a QC artifact: 951 genes have zero counts across all 1.24M cells and were retained, which an expression filter would not do. (b) The 489 Ensembl genes it omits are excluded by gene-model CLASS, not location or expression — 299 pseudogenes, 171 IG/TR receptor segments, 14 TEC, 5 other; 488 of 489 are on primary chromosomes and ZSCAPE keeps 462 genes on non-primary scaffolds, so it is not an assembly restriction. Dropping pseudogenes and rearranging immune-receptor segments is curation, not a stock Ensembl GTF — a third independent line of evidence (with the extended coordinates and the Ensembl-subset id space) for a curated extended-UTR annotation. Still no citation naming it. CAVEAT: gene metadata's num_cells_expressed is systematically HIGHER than the matrix supports (median ratio 1.0076, max 1.093, never lower across all 32,031 genes) despite both files claiming 1,241,018 cells. Recompute from the matrix if exact.
_provenance.zscape_supplementary: sources/supplementary/zscape-extra-metadata.xlsx — the paper's supplementary tables, 8 sheets. Highest-information single file in sources/. CONFIRMS THE PERTURBATION SPLIT FROM THE AUTHORS' OWN TABLE, not from naming convention: sheet 6_perturbation_info lists 28 rows using 'hgfa' / 'hgfa null', 'mafba' / 'mafba null', 'met' / 'met null', 'noto' / 'noto null', 'tbx16' / 'tbx16 null'. So obs[gene_target]'s '-mut' suffix IS the authors' stable NULL mutant line, and the sheet's 'Null Comparison (y/n)' column is 'y' on exactly those five crispant rows. 18 single + 5 double + 5 null = 28 labels = 23 distinct perturbations. Card group relabelled 'Stable null mutant line' to match the authors' term. TIMEPOINTS: sheet 1 gives four experiments — Time Series R1 (48/72/96), R2 (18-38 even, +42), R3 (40/42/44/46), and the perturbation experiment (18/24/36/48/72). Their union is EXACTLY the 18 numeric values in obs[timepoint], and the perturbation timepoints are a subset. The abstract's '19 timepoints' is still one more than any file accounts for — likely the blank level in the reference cell metadata. ALSO: hash enrichment thresholds (>3 for R1/R2, >5 for perturbations and R3) — this is the 'Supplementary Table 1' the Methods cite; 76 crRNA sequences over 27 gene entries (3 non-targeting controls), ~3 guides/gene, 7 failed phenotyping and 10 unused so the shipped pool is 66; rhAmpSeq genotyping primers for 26 genes; per-perturbation cell and individual counts (smallest is tbx16 null at 7,475 cells / 8 individuals). NAMING: obs writes 'wnt3a-wnt8' but the real second gene is wnt8a ('wnt3a; wnt8a'). Card chips keep the literal obs strings because that is what the data column contains. SCHEME vs DATA: sheet 2 documents the authored annotation scheme (36 tissue / 101 broad / 148 sub / 7 germ_layer) which does NOT equal the values realized in obs (34 / 99 / 156 / 7). Neither is wrong — different denominators. Card numbers stay measured from the data. MOST USEFUL TO US: sheet 2 carries a free-text 'evidence' column naming the marker genes behind each cell-type call (120 of 151 rows), and sheet 8 gives quantitative top markers for 151 cell_type_sub values. That is a far richer scoring target for the labeller than the label strings alone.
_provenance.chemfish_pipeline: CONFIRMED from the ChemFish Methods: 'Pipelines for generating count matrices from sci-RNA-seq3 sequencing data are available at github.com/bbi-lab/bbi-dmux and github.com/bbi-lab/bbi-sci', and 'data were processed using the Monocle3 (develop branch, v.1.3.1) workflow'. _provenance.daniocell: REFERENCE CONFIRMED from the Methods: GRCz11 / Ensembl release 99 with the Lawson Lab Zebrafish Transcriptome Annotation v4.3.2, 320 Ensembl-annotated pseudogenes removed, aligned with Cell Ranger 4.0.0 (STAR 2.5.1b), --expect-cells 6,000-21,250 per sample. New data is 10X Chromium 3' v3.1 + MULTI-seq; the 2018 Farrell Drop-seq cells were realigned against the same reference before merging. This is a DIFFERENT reference lineage from ZSCAPE/ChemFish — its 36,250 features do not correspond to their BBI-prepared 32,031. GENE UNIVERSE RECONSTRUCTED against the Lawson v4.3 we hold (v4.3.2 is UMass-only and bot-walled): v4.3 has 36,351 gene rows, 314 with an Ens99 pseudogene biotype (paper removes 320 in v4.3.2), leaving 36,031 vs the released 36,250 (+219). Cell Ranger feature-name de-duplication explains the shape: Lawson has 216 symbols occurring more than once over 458 rows, and exactly 242 DanioCell-only names are '<lawson symbol>.N' (e.g. 'HTRA2 (1 of many).10'); 32 more differ only by case. The residual 2,006 is the v4.3->v4.3.2 delta. QC VERIFIED CLEAN, unlike ChemFish: 0 cells with nGene<=200 (min exactly 201), 0 cells with percent.mt>=10 (max 9.999), no Doublet label present (only Bar1-Bar12 and Negative), 1 cell with nUMI_MS<20. The top-0.5%-features rule is not testable post-hoc. 59,013 cells lack MULTI-seq calls: 38,731 Drop-seq plus 20,282 non-hashed 10X. ACCOUNTING: 489,687 was a header-inclusive line count, real total 489,686. 63 distinct integer stages in the release (Drop-seq 10 at 3-12 hpf, 10X 53 at 14-120 hpf, no overlap) vs the paper's 62 — one unit, UNRESOLVED. 522 clust in metadata vs 521 annotation rows: 'ceph' (3,191 cells) is unannotated, so annotation covers 99.348% of cells. 498 clust and 19 tissues are the 18-96 hpf subset, not alternative atlas figures. CANONICAL CONVERSION UNRESOLVED: no script exists on the instance, and the README's '26,251 mapped' does not reproduce — the on-box gene_id_map_zf.tsv (31,312 entries) intersects DanioCell at 27,247, and neither equals the 30,121 features actually in daniocell_canonical.h5ad. All 30,121 do fall inside the ZSCAPE 32,031 space, so the conversion targeted it, but the mapping is not recorded. Regenerate with a logged conversion before depending on its exact gene set. CITATION CORRECTED: the dataset README cited Nature Communications 10.1038/s41467-024-50053-5, which Crossref 404s — the DOI does not exist. Correct venue is Developmental Cell 58, 3028-3047.e12 (2023), 10.1016/j.devcel.2023.11.001, PMID 37995681.
_provenance.zcl2: All facts from the authors' own release and the NAR paper: cells/genes from ZCDL.rdata (Seurat v4.0.2, 27,538 x 1,088,106); annotation tiers from ZCDL_cellinfo.csv (143 clusters / 41 cell_type / 10 cell_lineage, every cluster pure); genome/aligner/DGE quoted from the Methods (STAR, GRCz11, modified Drop-seq tools 1.12). Annotation release reads TBD because no paper, supplement or repo states a GTF or Ensembl release -- the namespace is 93.6% present in the Ensembl 99 symbol set, which dates it to *an* Ensembl release and no further. Accession names both GEO series because the paper cites only GSE198832, whose zebrafish subseries covers 21d+22m; 24hpf/72hpf/3m are GSE178150 under a different SuperSeries. Full record: ZCL2/sources/README.md.
_provenance.micdrop: Cells/genes/tiers read from the deposited GEO artifacts, not the paper text: 226,492 x 17 cell metadata (74 curated_cell_type2, 3 cell_class, 179 predicted.id) and the 32,520 Gene Expression + 204 CRISPR Guide Capture features.tsv. Genome reads GRCz11 but Annotation reads TBD deliberately: the paper and GEO both claim a Lawson v4.3.2 reference, yet the deposited feature universe is EXACTLY the Ensembl GRCz11 gene set (32,520/32,520 identical to our release-114 GTF) while the Lawson v4.3 GTF shares 0 of its 36,351 LL ids -- so the claim is contradicted and the Ensembl release cannot be dated (the zebrafish gene set is unchanged from release 99 to 114). Raw processing records Cell Ranger v7 because that is what all 36 GEO samples state; the paper's Methods name no version at all. Controls read tyr because Supplementary Data 3 names the four control guides tyr-1..4 while the deposited feature reference calls the same four sequences Non-Targeting. Genotype-assigned counts are ours from `class`; the paper's 135,881 is not reproducible from any released artifact. Full record: MICDropSeq/sources/README.md.
_provenance.celloracle: Cells/genes/design read from the GEO deposit, not the paper. 394,459 cells over the 30 Danio rerio samples of GSE145298's 31 (GSM4314394 perturbseq_ieps is Mus musculus). Genome reads GRCz11 per GEO; Annotation reads a reconstructed rule with release TBD because neither paper nor GEO names a GTF: the 25,107-feature universe is reproduced EXACTLY, in set and in GTF order, by Ensembl GRCz11 protein_coding restricted to the primary assembly (chr 1-25 + MT, 325 scaffold genes dropped), and releases 99/102/114 are identical under that rule so it cannot be dated. Not Lawson: 0 of its 36,351 LL ids appear. Cell Ranger v5.0.1 agrees between the paper Methods and GEO. Schema reads NONE DEPOSITED because the tar contains only barcodes/features/matrix -- no labels, embeddings or Seurat object. Controls are split three ways because tyr is an F0 crispant with real Cas9 cutting, not a neutral control. Full record: CellOracle/sources/README.md.
_provenance.tahoe: All figures measured from the deposit, not the paper. 100,648,790 cells is the sum of our 14 plate H5ADs AND the row count of obs_metadata.parquet; 95,624,334 is pass_filter=='full' and exactly the Hugging Face expression split's num_examples, so '100M' is branding and both numbers are stated. Controls: DMSO_TF covers all 700 plate x cell-line combinations. Trap: 'Trametinib (DMSO_TF solvate)' is a MEK inhibitor, not a control. moa/target/approval fields are GPT-4o-generated, not curated. zscape_commit_gold.name: ZSCAPE Commit Gold
zscape_commit_gold.summary: The Commit benchmark cut: ZSCAPE's published 112-cluster gold set at 48 hpf, control arm only. Clustering is given and frozen, so three personalities label each fixed cluster from a ZFA option menu and score by exact ZFA-ID match. Not blind — we hold the answer key on-instance.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: inherited: Commit Gold is a cut of the same published ZSCAPE data and carries the identical 32,031-gene feature universe.

zscape.name: ZSCAPE
zscape.summary: The Trapnell-lab whole-embryo knockout atlas: 28 gene knockouts against six control arms, spanning 18 to 96 hpf. We re-cluster from scratch with recursive per-compartment clustering, then score our de-novo names against the authors' published germ-layer, tissue, broad and sub labels.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: pipeline reconstruction + exact feature/coordinate fingerprint. No ZSCAPE-specific run manifest naming the GTF recovered.

chemfish.name: ChemFish
chemfish.summary: Barkan et al. chemical-screen atlas — eight pathway-blocking compounds across three timepoints, hitting Hedgehog, retinoic acid, BMP, Notch, TGF-β, FGF and Wnt. We re-cluster the 48 hpf window de-novo and score against the authors' native tissue and cell-type labels.

reference.extension: +500 bp 3′, strand-aware — clipped where it would overlap a same-strand gene
reference.confidence: ChemFish's own BPCells row_names are byte-identical to ZSCAPE's 32,031-gene set. Coordinates not independently re-tested; same lab, same assay, same reference build.

daniocell.name: DanioCell
daniocell.summary: Farrell-lab dense developmental reference: 489,686 cells over 63 stages from 3 to 120 hpf, nothing perturbed. 10X Chromium plus realigned 2018 Drop-seq, MULTI-seq hashed. Populations are in-situ-validated, and 521 clusters carry author annotations with ZFA ontology IDs.

reference.processing: Cell Ranger mkref · 320 Ensembl pseudogenes removed
reference.extension: none — Cell Ranger default, no 3′ extension
reference.confidence: stated directly in the Methods. Distinct reference lineage from ZSCAPE/ChemFish — Lawson v4.3.2 via Cell Ranger, not the BBI Ensembl-99 +500 bp build, so the 36,250 features do NOT correspond to their 32,031.

zebrahub.name: Zebrahub
zebrahub.notRunnable: Not a labelling target — 10X droplet, so it doesn't integrate with the combinatorial-indexing atlases (ZSCAPE / ChemFish / MegaFIN). Gene IDs are not a barrier: 31,569 ENSDARG are shared with them.

timepoints.highlightTitle: 2 dpf = 48 hpf — the common join point across the atlases

zebrahub.summary: Wild-type developmental reference spanning 10 hpf to 10 dpf across 40 embryos, annotated to 154 fine ZFA classes. Reference only — 10X droplet keeps it from integrating with the combinatorial-indexing atlases we label, though its gene IDs do overlap.

megafin_parse.name: MegaFin Part 1 — Parse Processed

perturbations.summary: 45 SMALL MOLECULES + SORAFENIB (POS. CTRL) · 1 µM & 5 µM · 3 WELLS QC-REMOVED

megafin_parse.summary: Large-scale anti-angiogenesis screen: 45 small molecules at 1 and 5 µM plus a Sorafenib positive control, 96 conditions and no replicates, TU wildtype dosed 24–48 hpf, 6 embryos per well. The Parse/Trailmaker processing of the library, in ENSDARG. A labelling target, not a benchmark.

megafin.name: MegaFin Part 1 — ZSB, June 14th

perturbations.summary: 45 SMALL MOLECULES + SORAFENIB (POS. CTRL) · 1 µM & 5 µM · 3 WELLS QC-REMOVED

megafin.summary: The same anti-angiogenesis screen as the Parse build — 45 small molecules at 1 and 5 µM plus Sorafenib, dosed 24–48 hpf — rebuilt from the manually denoised Lawson object and clustered recursively. Shares no cell barcodes with its sibling, so the two are an independent check.

minifin.name: MiniFin

perturbations.summary: 3 COMPOUNDS · 1 µM EACH · SORAFENIB = ANTI-ANGIOGENIC POS. CTRL

minifin.summary: Pilot validating Parse Evercode combinatorial barcoding in whole embryos, aimed at angiogenesis: Sorafenib (VEGFR/PDGFR/Raf, anti-angiogenic positive control) against Orlistat (FAS) and Dapagliflozin (SGLT2), all 1 µM, dosed 24–48 hpf, 12 replicates each. TU wildtype, 6 embryos per well.

zcl2.name: ZCL 2.0
zcl2.notRunnable: Viable labelling target — the full 143-cluster hierarchy lives in the authors' companion ZCDL_cellinfo.csv, not in the Seurat object, which is why we previously recorded this dataset as unannotated. Caveats: Microwell-seq is shallow (median 872 UMI / 475 genes per cell) and the released atlas is pre-QC.
zcl2.workingSlice: 1,082,680 annotated · 5,426 cells carry no published label
zcl2.summary: Wild-type life-span atlas from 24 hpf to 22 months — the only zebrafish reference here reaching adult and aged animals. 143 annotated clusters across 10 lineages. Coverage is shallow and the released object is pre-QC, so treat its thresholds as unapplied.

micdrop.name: MIC-Drop-seq
micdrop.notRunnable: Annotation was transferred from DanioCell (21–26 hpf) and then hand-curated, so its labels are not independent evidence about DanioCell. 161 of 179 transfer labels match a DanioCell annotation row exactly.
micdrop.workingSlice: 138,767 genotype-assigned · 87,725 Not Determined · pilot is a separate 21,994-cell object

pipeline.raw: Cell Ranger v7 (GEO) · paper states no version

micdrop.summary: Pooled CRISPR screen: 50 transcription factors disrupted across ~1,000 embryos, genotyped in situ by captured gRNAs. 226,492 cells at 24 hpf over 74 cell types. The only dataset here pairing a per-cell genotype with a whole-embryo phenotype.

celloracle.name: CellOracle
celloracle.notRunnable: No cell-type annotations exist in the deposit — GEO ships Cell Ranger matrices only. The paper's labels were transferred from Farrell et al. 2018 and then propagated WT→perturbed, but no label, embedding or Seurat object is distributed.
celloracle.workingSlice: 30 zebrafish samples of 31 — GSM4314394 is mouse and excluded
celloracle.annotation: Ensembl protein-coding, primary assembly · release TBD

timepoints.highlightTitle: 10 hpf — every perturbation is assayed here; 6/8 hpf are wild-type reference only

groups.label: F0 crispants (Cas9 RNP at 0 hpf)
items: tyr — the paper's injection-control baseline, but a real crispant, not neutral

celloracle.summary: Zebrafish crispants and flh mutants at 10 hpf against a 6/8/10 hpf wild-type reference — the observed perturbation ground truth behind CellOracle's in silico knockouts. Ships matrices only: no cell-type labels, and tyr is a crispant rather than a neutral control.

tahoe.name: Tahoe-100M
tahoe.notRunnable: Human, not zebrafish — a cross-species reference for method development, never pooled with the zebrafish atlases. There are no cell-type labels: the biological identity axis is the cell line, assigned by genetic demultiplexing.
tahoe.workingSlice: 95,624,334 pass_filter='full' — the public expression split. Our 14 plate H5ADs hold all 100.6M, a superset by 5,024,456 cells
tahoe.line: 50 cancer cell lines, pooled per well

items: DMSO_TF — match drug == "DMSO_TF" exactly; a substring match on "DMSO" also captures Trametinib (DMSO_TF solvate), a MEK inhibitor

tahoe.summary: Giga-scale chemical perturbation: 50 cancer cell lines pooled per well, 1,138 drug×dose combinations, 100.6M cells. Every plate×line pair has a matched vehicle control. Its pseudobulk-DE companion is the template for how we would summarise the zebrafish perturbation data.

replogle.name: Replogle
replogle.notRunnable: Human, not zebrafish. The authors' primary release plus the previously held scPerturb redistributions are both available locally. Gene-filtered to ~8.2–8.7k features — so it is a method reference, not a labelling target.
replogle.workingSlice: 3 objects: K562 GWPS 1,989,578 · K562 essential 310,385 · RPE1 247,914
replogle.annotation: TBD — scPerturb-processed; ENSG present in var

schema.status: NO CELL TYPES — one cell line per object

controls.summary: non-targeting 'control' · 97,504 cells across the three objects

replogle.summary: Genome-scale CRISPRi Perturb-seq in two human cell lines: 9,866 targets genome-wide in K562 plus essential-gene screens in K562 and RPE1. Single-target only. The canonical example of a one-context, many-perturbation design — the mirror image of our zebrafish data.
